note: Newest first. where: live = the normal app, test = the test version (/test/), android = the Android app.

entries.title: Back button
items: The phone's back button now steps back inside the app (close a pop-up, leave a settings page, back to the set list ...) instead of closing the app. Only on the start screen does it leave the app.

entries.title: Updates without reinstalling
items: The app now checks for a newer version by itself (when you open it or come back to it) and shows “A new version is ready” - tap Update.
The Android app shows “Download” for a new version: install it over the old one, your cards stay.

entries.title: What's new
items: This list: see what changed in each update, with the older updates below it.

entries.title: Camera screen in the app's style
items: Before the camera starts you see a card frame in your theme colours instead of a grey box.

entries.title: Every printing, languages and graded cards
items: The scan result now finds all printings of a card (not just the first ten or so), with “All printings” and a search box.
Not in the list? Type the set code and number printed on the card - it is looked up, or added as you typed it.
New “EN” button next to Foil: mark the language (Japanese, German, French ...) and graded copies (PSA, BGS, CGC, SGC ... with the grade).
Each language and grade is its own entry in My cards, with a small badge, and can have its own price.

entries.title: Android app (test)
items: Nightvault Pocket as an Android app, with Google's text reader on the phone: faster and much better at reading card names.
Settings → Scanning can switch back to the web reader to compare.
Files you export open the Android share menu (Drive, mail, Files).

entries.title: Better at reading card names
items: Names on coloured or silver bars are read word by word, with a sharper second read and a taller box when the card is not exactly in the frame.
Pokémon cards are found by the number at the bottom (like 150/217) - also when the name cannot be read.

entries.title: World of Warcraft TCG card text
items: Card text for about 7,800 WoW TCG cards, read from card pictures - search it in the deck builder.

entries.title: Two-way sync with Nightvault on the PC
items: Added, fewer and removed cards travel both ways, exactly once.
Decks, wishlist, your own prices and the order of price sources are shared too.

entries.title: New icons
items: The icons inside the app are redrawn in the style of the new logo.

entries.title: New look
items: New app icon: fanned cards under a constellation.
Splash screen with the logo in the colours of your theme.
Home screen with tiles for scanning, binder, decks, upcoming releases and syncing; settings behind the gear.
Game emblems, and your own logo or picture per game.

entries.title: Decks
items: Deck builder for every game: search by name or card text, with filters (cost, colour, type, rarity ...), sets and “cards I have”.
Cost curve, value, what you own and what is missing; paste and copy deck lists.
Deck rules per deck (deck size, sideboard, copies of a card), with the usual rules for known games.
Add to a deck from the binder and the scanner.

entries.title: Prices from several sources
items: Cardmarket, TCGplayer and your own price, in the order you choose - no price at the first source, then the next.
Prices sheet per card with every source, shop links and eBay sold listings.
Daily prices for many more games, also old out-of-print ones.

entries.title: Binder and releases
items: Set lists grouped by product type (main sets, Commander, Secret Lair, decks, promos ...).
Upcoming releases: card game sets coming out soon, updated every day.
Star Wars CCG sets with their official names, codes and dates.
Big pictures and full card details; card text read by Nightvault on the PC.

entries.title: Test version
items: A separate test version at /test/ to try new things first; your real collection is not touched.

entries.title: Nightvault Pocket
items: Scan cards with the phone camera: one card, a whole binder page, or quick scanning card after card.
Magic, Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Lorcana, Star Wars Unlimited, One Piece, Riftbound and many more games, plus any game by hand.
My cards and a binder per set, with prices, foils, a wishlist and a trade list.
Scan templates for unusual card layouts, and card backs it learns.
Backups, and export to Nightvault on the PC.
